capabilities: Add ARIA roles, names, and states to div-based UI controls (ribbon, tabs, file tree, modals, palettes, settings)
Restore keyboard operability with roving tab order, focus traps, and arrow-key navigation
Restore a visible focus indicator and honor OS reduced-motion settings
Announce toast notices and caret line numbers through polite live regions
Apply mobile screen-reader retrofits (TalkBack/VoiceOver roles, labels, and focus containment)
extras: Still in beta and installed via BRAT or manual download rather than the Community Plugins store. Version 0.7.0 changed the plugin ID from a11y-enhancer, so the old copy must be uninstalled separately or both will run and double every fix. Some version-compatibility deferrals are checked against Obsidian's code and release notes but not yet verified in a live keyboard-only or screen-reader pass.
intentEvidence: retrofits WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility onto Obsidian's interface at runtime — no wait for upstream
problem: Obsidian's interface is built from divs with little ARIA, few native controls, and state carried only by CSS classes, making it largely unusable with a keyboard or screen reader.

relations.evidence: BRAT pulls the latest GitHub release, so you get updates automatically.

summary: Runtime DOM-patching plugin that retrofits WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility onto Obsidian's UI: keyboard operability, ARIA roles, focus ring, reduced motion, and screen-reader announcements.
